candidate_profile.description: The candidate immediately sees that higher market share is not necessarily good, diagnoses the business as a participant in a shrinking industry under severe pricing pressure, and gives a crisp recommendation centered on cost reduction, leverage, and diversification.
behaviour_rules: Begin with a concise recap and explicitly state that market share is only meaningful in the context of total market size and industry economics.
Use a sharp profitability framework to separate volume, price, and cost drivers.
Establish quickly that costs are stable, so declining profit must come from weaker revenue quality rather than cost inflation.
Recognize that slight volume gains above industry average are not enough to offset price compression.
Interpret competitor exits as evidence that the market is saturated and declining, not as proof of healthy competitive advantage.
Connect lower preservative demand directly to consumer preference for fresh food and a shrinking end market.
Conclude that the client has gained share mostly because rivals exited while everyone is lowering price to survive, reducing margin per unit.
Recommend cost reduction, collaborative leverage with the remaining industry where feasible, and diversification into chemical products with stronger demand trends.

expected_issues: May not define the exact diversification targets because the case only points generically to other chemical categories.
Could still be pushed for implementation prioritization after the strategic diagnosis.
expected_feedback_points: Excellent interpretation of market share in context.
Excellent diagnosis of shrinking-market price pressure.
Excellent elimination of cost growth as the core issue.
Excellent connection between competitor exits, lower demand, and weaker unit margins.
Excellent recommendation to cut costs, improve leverage, and diversify into more attractive chemicals.
